prompt: Match each project file to what belongs in it.
right: What the project is and how to run it
Files that should never be committed
explain: A README is the first thing anyone opens, including you in six months.

prompt: Match each stage of a project to what you produce.
right: Working features, one at a time
A list of what it should do and what it should not
A demo and an honest account of what is unfinished
A short written case for the idea
explain: Deciding what a project will NOT do is planning work, and skipping it is how a capstone runs out of time.

prompt: Which of these make a project easier for someone else to run?
choices: A README with the exact commands to start it
Pinning the versions of packages you depend on
Keeping all the code in one long file
Handling a missing input file with a clear message
explain: One long file is easier to write and harder for everyone afterwards, including the person who wrote it.

label: Complete the guard so this file can be both run and imported.
prompt: Complete the guard so this file can be both run and imported.
explain: This is what lets another file import your functions without your whole program starting up.

label: Fill both blanks so a bad number is reported instead of crashing.
prompt: Fill both blanks so a bad number is reported instead of crashing.
explain: int() raises ValueError on text it cannot convert, and catching that one by name says what you expected to go wrong.

prompt: Put these steps in the order a project is built.
items: Decide what the project will and will not do
Set up the folder and a place to run it
Build one core feature and check it works
Write the README and present it
explain: Scope first: every step after it is cheaper once you know what you are not building.
